name: SA05
hook: Super Aguri's first Formula 1 car was a secondhand 2002 Arrows, because the rules barred the car the team really wanted.
story: Picture Aguri Suzuki in November 2005. He has a new Japanese team, Honda engines and a simple plan. He will race a car from Honda's own works team. Then the rival teams open the Concorde Agreement. No team, it says, may race parts designed by another constructor. The plan is dead, and the first race is four months away. So Suzuki goes shopping for history. Paul Stoddart has a few Arrows A23s, cars from 2002, left over after Arrows went bust. Suzuki buys them. His engineers fit Honda's new 2.4-litre V8, cut fresh cooling inlets, and add a new engine cover, diffuser and rear wing for the 2006 rules. In February the car shakes down on an airfield in Gloucestershire, painted plain white. At its first test in Barcelona, it stops after three laps. Then Bahrain. Takuma Sato brings it home eighteenth. A rulebook killed the car Suzuki wanted. A four-year-old ghost went racing instead.
description: The Super Aguri SA05 was the first car of Super Aguri F1, the Japanese team Aguri Suzuki founded in late 2005 with Honda's backing. Barred from using a car built by another constructor, the team took the 2002 Arrows A23, designed by Mike Coughlan and Sergio Rinland, and reworked it for 2006 under former Arrows engineer Mark Preston. It ran Honda's RA806E V8. Takuma Sato and Yuji Ide drove it for the first eleven rounds, before the updated SA06 took over at the German Grand Prix.
